item.title: Nepal disaster: fake and AI images flood social media as deaths mount
item.description: As deadly floods hit the Nepal-China border, social media is being flooded with fake and misleading footage. In Truth or Fake, Vedika Bahl goes through viral videos falsely linked to the disaster, including AI-generated content and old recycled footage from India, Chile and Alaska. Some posts have racked up millions of views online, exploiting the tragedy to drive engagement for easy clicks or further perpetuate conspiracy theories. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Nepal‑Tibet disaster linked to climate change—a glaciologist explains
item.description: The cause of the huge floods and debris flow on the border between Nepal and Tibet, which have caused hundreds of deaths, appears to have been an ice avalanche—the result of a huge piece of a glacier collapsing and cascading down the mountain more than 1,000 meters (3,281 feet) to the valley floor. The Conversation asked Jonathan Bamber, a professor of glaciology at the University of Bristol, about the risks of glaciers melting faster than ever. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Nepal floods 'unprecedented', requires new 'engineering approaches, risk-sensitive urban planning'
item.description: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome Dr. Basanta Raj Adhikari, Director of the Center for Disaster Studies at Tribhuvan University’s Institute of Engineering. He describes the disaster as an illustration of the limits of conventional prevention in the Himalayas. With flood velocities estimated at 170 to 180 kilometres per hour and hazards ranging from ice and snow avalanches to glacial lake outburst floods, he argues that comprehensive monitoring of Nepal’s exceptionally steep and complex mountain terrain is effectively impossible. Yet Adhikari’s analysis is not fatalistic. Instead, he shifts… Fuente: France 24 - English.

At the centre of his desired policies was a “BYO power” requirement – a condition that all new datacentres would be powered by 100% renewable electricity. item.description: Un equipo de France 24 visitó la localidad de Sinchaur, en el distrito nepalés de Nuwako, donde cientos de familias fueron afectadas por la riada. Algunos habitantes pudieron rescatar algunas de sus pertenencias, pero otros lo perdieron absolutamente todo y tuvieron que alejarse de la zona con las manos vacías. A medida que el riesgo de una segunda inundación crece, las autoridades hacen nuevos llamados de evacuación de los residentes, pero hay quienes se niegan a irse de sus hogares por temor a sufrir robos durante su ausencia. item.title: Vanished Texas bird island is back, with 2,500 pairs of birds
item.description: After years of erosion and extreme weather, Dickinson Bay's lost islands have seen a remarkable revival. Spearheaded by the Galveston Bay Foundation and U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, habitat restoration efforts have successfully created new nesting habitats for over 2,500 pairs of waterbirds. This revitalization not only boosts local biodiversity but also creates job opportunities and enhances economic activity through recreational fishing and improved oyster reefs. item.description: La sequía y las olas de calor que han castigado Francia a lo largo de los últimos meses han tenido una consecuencia inesperada: están obligando al país a pensar nuevas formas de elaborar sus quesos más populares. La lógica es sencilla. Menos lluvia se traduce en menos forraje, prados amarillentos y menos pasto con el que alimentar el ganado. Para paliarlo, las autoridades han decidido hacer de tripas corazón y relajar las estrictitas normas que deben cumplir los productores que elaboran los quesos Beaufort o Comté con denominación de origen.
